subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw define a versioned core/plugin response-gate API that can fail closed before final output delivery, or should this remain limited to plugin-owned pre-tool, prompt, and output-filter policies?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses security policy, plugin API, config, audit, retry, and agent/channel delivery semantics; source inspection shows no existing seam that can safely satisfy it without choosing the product contract first.

options.title: Design core response-gate API
options.body: Approve a versioned core/plugin seam for mandatory-tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed final delivery, bounded retries, and audit records before implementation.

options.title: Keep policy packs plugin-only
options.body: Leave domain policies in plugins or ClawHub and do not add a hard final-delivery gate unless a narrower missing API is proposed.

options.title: Split narrower contracts
options.body: Track outbound user approval, mandatory tool accounting, and audit logging as separate design items before coding.

recommendation.title: Design core response-gate API
recommendation.body: Approve a versioned core/plugin seam for mandatory-tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed final delivery, bounded retries, and audit records before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current code ownership is the plugin hook/API and before_agent_finalize path where a response-gate seam would likely be designed.
